components.gap: LR001-C2: the held preprint's Section 3 states that rules (A), (T) and (I) have no classical counterparts (p. 12); this historical claim is absent from the route (syllogistic-inference.tex lines 122-129 describe A, T and I without it, and no other route file states it). | LR001-C2: the preprint justifies rule (T) by noting that without it there would be no way to derive the formula every p is a p from the empty set of premises (p. 12); the route omits this justificatory claim (syllogistic-inference.tex line 122 says only that T supplies reflexive inclusion; the premise-free derivation in w02-p02-001 lines 408-409 and annex lines 226-228 is not the necessity claim). | LR001-C2: the preprint gives the reasons the redundant rule (D1) is kept, namely ease of use and a more transparent relationship to the relational system of its Section 4.2 (p. 13); syllogistic-inference.tex line 137 says only that D1 is retained in its source sheet, so the stated justification is omitted. | LR001-C2: the preprint's hypothesis that Phi is a set of universal formulas (definition of the closure V^Phi and Lemmas 3.3, 3.4 and 3.5, pp. 14-15) is not stated in def:p02-syllogistic-literal-closure or in Lemmas thm:p02-syllogistic-closure and thm:p02-syllogistic-extension (syllogistic-inference.tex lines 171-196); as written, the second sentence of thm:p02-syllogistic-extension asserts a one-element model of an arbitrary Phi (false for Phi containing an existential formula such as Some p is a q with the closed set of non-p), while its annex proof (annex lines 212-218) establishes the model only for universal premises.
